intended_object: The image of the sign (signature) map (𝒪_K)^× → ∏_{real places} {±1}, u ↦ (sign σ_w(u))_w: the subgroup of sign patterns at the real places that units of the ring of integers realize. This is inferred from the docstring and from the module's use for the kernel of the map from the narrow ray class group to the ordinary one.
explanation:
The definition is `MonoidHom.range` of the library's `NumberField.unitSignature`. That map is `fieldUnitSignature` composed with the inclusion (𝒪_K)^× → K^×. `fieldUnitSignature` sends a unit u, at each real place w, to the class of `embedding_of_isReal w u` in ℝ^× / ℝ_{>0}, which is the two-element sign group. So the definition is exactly the subgroup of ∏_{w real} {±1} made of the sign vectors of global units. This is the standard object whose cokernel gives the kernel of Cl⁺(K) → Cl(K).

The `@`-explicit `Pi.group` instance only fixes how the instances are elaborated and does not change the mathematical content. Degenerate cases also come out right: for a totally complex field the index type is empty, so the subgroup is the trivial group.

The setting is the natural one, since unit signatures are a notion about the integer units of a number field. The `omit [NumberField K]` only weakens the assumptions on `K`. I found no Mathlib definition of this subgroup or of the signature map in this Mathlib version. The library has a version for general orders (`NumberFieldOrder.unitSignatures`), but this definition is the standard case of the maximal order and is not a narrowing of any Mathlib notion.
